description:
We are Galaxy Divers. 

We dive into the galaxy to explore and explain what's really going on in our surroundings which we can't see just by our eyes.
summary:
Our tool organises SPHEREx data for easy access and decoding for users worldwide.

It links SPHEREx data with an interactive sky map, allowing users to locate sky patches by entering coordinates. Additional features are included for user convenience.

The tool has been validated using the provided targets.
details:
Galaxy Divers – SPHEREx Time-Domain Explorer

1. Project Overview

Galaxy Divers is an interactive astronomy web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, inspired by the challenge "Planet X and SPHEREx."

The main objective is to make astronomical observations more accessible by allowing users to explore the infrared universe and investigate how celestial objects and regions of the sky change over time.

SPHEREx observes the entire sky in 102 spectral channels of near-infrared light. By examining observations from different periods, scientists can investigate changing brightness, moving objects, and unusual astronomical phenomena.

Our platform aims to simplify this process through an accessible and interactive scientific workspace.

2. Main Features

Interactive Sky Explorer

Users can enter Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates to explore specific regions of the sky using an interactive astronomical map.

SPHEREx Observation Explorer

The application connects with astronomical archive services to search for available SPHEREx observations and retrieve relevant observation metadata.

Multi-Epoch Image Comparison

Users can investigate the same region of the sky across different observation dates. The comparison workspace is designed to support split-view comparison, blink mode, image overlays, and difference imaging.

102-Band Infrared Exploration

The platform introduces an interface for exploring SPHEREx's 102 nominal infrared spectral channels, helping users understand how astronomical objects can appear differently across wavelengths.

Scientific Analysis and Visualization

Our planned analysis workspace includes image comparison results, brightness measurements, source detection, statistical graphs, spectral visualizations, and candidate investigation tools.

Planet X Investigation

Users can explore selected astronomical targets and investigate unusual observations. Potential detections are treated as candidates requiring further scientific verification, rather than confirmed discoveries.

Research and Learning Resources

Galaxy Divers also aims to support students and astronomy enthusiasts through educational resources, scientific explanations, and interactive exploration tools.

3. Technologies and Tools Used

We developed the platform using modern full-stack technologies:

  • Frontend: React.js, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3 and Vite.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Astronomy and Scientific Computing: Astropy, Astroquery, NumPy and SciPy.
  • Sky Visualization: Aladin Lite.
  • Data Visualization: Interactive charts and scientific image visualizations.
  • External Data: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) and publicly available astronomical datasets.
  • Deployment: Vercel for the frontend and Render for the backend.
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub.

4. Creativity and Innovation

The creative idea behind Galaxy Divers is to transform complex astronomical observations into an accessible visual experience.

Instead of requiring users to manually examine large astronomical datasets, our platform provides a centralized environment for coordinate-based exploration, observation discovery, image comparison, and scientific investigation.

The time-based comparison concept is particularly important because it allows users to investigate changes between observations and identify interesting candidates for further research.

5. Intended Impact

Galaxy Divers aims to make time-domain astronomy more accessible to students, researchers, educators, and space enthusiasts.

By simplifying access to astronomical observations and providing interactive scientific visualization tools, we hope to encourage public participation in astronomy and help users better understand the changing infrared universe.

Our long-term vision is to develop Galaxy Divers into a collaborative citizen-science platform where people can explore real astronomical observations, investigate unusual objects, and contribute to scientific discovery.
